top_story.headline: Marine Band wants to rent an Alexandria community college concert hall without competition
top_story.dek: The notice of intent covers 12 concerts and 6 recording days from January to August 2027.
paragraphs: The U.S. Marine Band, through the Department of the Navy, intends to award a sole-source contract to Virginia Community College System for the Rachel M. Schlesinger Concert Hall and Arts Center in Alexandria, Virginia.

The agency says only one source is available because outreach events require advance scheduling and venue availability can't be guaranteed otherwise. No value is stated. USAspending shows no federal contract on record under this vendor name.

sections.headline: U.S. Marine Band plans no-bid rental of an Alexandria concert hall for 12 concerts
paragraphs: One new justification today, posted as a Special Notice rather than under the Justification category; one repeat from an earlier edition was left out.

blocks.title: Marine Band to rent Northern Virginia community college concert hall without competition for 12 concerts and 6 recording days
meta: only one company can do it
Department of the Navy (Marine Barracks Washington)
blocks.text: The U.S. Marine Band intends to sole-source 18 days of rental at the Rachel M. Schlesinger Concert Hall and Arts Center in Alexandria, Virginia, from Virginia Community College System for concerts and recordings between January and August 2027. The agency says marketing and community outreach require advance scheduling, and venue availability cannot be guaranteed without prior coordination. USAspending shows no federal contract on record under this vendor name; the document is marked controlled unclassified information and cites the simplified acquisition threshold, which suggests a small-dollar buy, though no value is stated.

sections.headline: $144 million Customs and Border Protection facility in Jacksonville tops new awards
paragraphs: From this morning's edition: USAspending.gov is pulled once a day.

7 new awards of $2 million or more were reported; the largest is a $144 million construction contract for U.S. Customs and Border Protection. None is tied to the White House or the Executive Office of the President.

blocks.title: Southwest Valley Constructors wins $144 million to build a Customs and Border Protection facility in Jacksonville
blocks.text: Southwest Valley Constructors Co received a $144 million order on September 30, 2026 for construction of a U.S. Customs and Border Protection facility in Jacksonville, Florida, classified as construction of administrative facilities and service buildings. It is an order under an existing contract vehicle.
Other new awards of $2 million or more

items: Blue Cord Design and Construction, LLC — $12,974,316, Department of Veterans Affairs: renovation of interventional radiology suites (award).
Standard Communications Inc — $8,450,000, Department of Veterans Affairs: design-build removal and replacement of a hospital nurse call system (award).
After Action Medical and Dental Supply, LLC — $4,168,899, Department of Veterans Affairs: medical and surgical supply orders placed in September 2026 (award).

Guidehouse Inc. — $4,023,683, Department of Agriculture (Office of the Chief Financial Officer): human capital modernization and transformation support for the department's human resources office (award).
Ascellon Corporation — $2,867,436, Department of Veterans Affairs: first-quarter fiscal 2027 surveys of state veterans homes and community living centers (award).
Excelsior Defense, Inc — $2,867,232, Department of Veterans Affairs: security guard services (award).

NaphCare LLC — $300,000, Department of Justice (Federal Bureau of Prisons): comprehensive medical services at the Allenwood federal correctional complex; the description cites Executive Order 14398 (award).

blocks.text: 25 new awards under $2 million were screened; 1 was flagged and listed above, 0 flagged were cut for length.
